name: Texas Disposal Systems
summary: Roll-off dumpsters in College Station, Bryan, Wellborn, Millican, Kurten, Snook, and parts of Navasota and Caldwell. The College Station page names a project use for each size and says the price is customized. No dollar rate is published.
accepted: Most common household and construction debris, including furniture, appliances with Freon removed, lumber, drywall, roofing shingles, concrete, rock, dirt, brush, and general household junk.
prohibited: Hazardous waste, paint, motor oil, gasoline, pesticides, tires, and batteries.

offers.fit: Listed as a 20-yard container. The page lists dimensions 22L x 8W x 3.5H and does not name the unit. It says the container holds 5,000-8,000 lbs. Best use on the page: single-room renovations, flooring removal, deck demolition, and moderate landscaping. The FAQ says a 20-yard is sufficient for most single-room renovations.
offers.shortNote: Pricing is customized. No dollar price is published. The size section says it holds 5,000-8,000 lbs.
offers.note: College Station roll-off page lists a 20-yard container. Dimensions on the page: 22L x 8W x 3.5H. The page does not name the unit. The size section says it holds 5,000-8,000 lbs of debris. Best use on the page: single-room renovations, flooring removal, deck demolition, and moderate landscaping debris. The FAQ says a 20-yard is sufficient for most single-room renovations. The pricing section says the price is customized. No dollar price, included day count, per-ton fee, or extra day fee is published. The page says delivery, haul-away, and pickup are part of the rental. It also says a weight allowance is included and that an overweight load can add a charge. It does not publish the allowance in tons or the charge.

offers.fit: Listed as a 30-yard container. The page lists dimensions 22L x 8W x 6H and does not name the unit. It says the container holds 8,000-12,000 lbs. The FAQ recommends a 30-yard for a multi-room remodel, a kitchen gut, or a full home renovation.
